title: Re-entrant parity-time phase transitions in locally coupled ring resonators
authors: Nguyen Duc Anh Quan, Le Xuan The Tai, Doan Quang Tri, Pawel S. Jung, Marek Trippenbach, Nguyen Viet Hung
abstract: We investigate two parity-time-symmetric ring resonators coupled over a finite angular region described by a super-Gaussian profile. In the linear regime, analytical spectra are obtained in the homogeneous-coupling and fixed-amplitude narrow-contact limits, while the finite-width problem is treated numerically. Local coupling introduces nonzero spatial Fourier components that mix angular harmonics and lift the degeneracy of counterpropagating modes, resolving each excited doublet into parity-dependent branches. Collisions among these branches generate multiple exceptional-point boundaries and disconnected broken-PT domains. The resulting phase diagrams exhibit re-entrant unbroken-broken-unbroken transitions when the gain-loss strength, coupling width, or peak coupling amplitude is varied. The numerical spectra continuously recover both analytical limits. In the nonlinear regime, selected ground and excited linear modes are used as seeds for adiabatic propagation into finite-amplitude Kerr waveforms that remain dynamically persistent over the simulated observation interval for finite ranges of nonlinear strength. These results show that the spatial profile of inter-resonator coupling provides a geometric means of controlling multimode PT transitions and selecting dynamically accessible nonlinear waveforms in coupled-ring systems.
summary: The paper analyzes how local coupling modifies parity-time symmetry in coupled ring resonators, revealing complex re-entrant phase transitions. By varying geometric parameters like coupling width, the system's PT phase can be controlled. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that these spatial couplings allow for the selection and stabilization of specific nonlinear light waveforms.
main_problem: The study investigates re-entrant parity-time (PT) phase transitions occurring within locally coupled ring resonators.
main_result: The spatial profile of the inter-resonator coupling provides a geometric mechanism to control multimode PT transitions and select dynamically accessible nonlinear waveforms in these coupled systems.
method: The analysis combines linear spectral calculations using Fourier collocation with nonlinear dynamics simulated via adiabatic propagation into Kerr waveforms.
model_or_system: The system consists of two identical ring resonators ($\psi_1, \psi_2$) coupled by a local super-Gaussian profile $\kappa(x)$, governed by coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations incorporating gain and loss.
key_observables: Spectral growth rate ($\Gamma_{\max}$), which diagnoses the PT phase (real spectrum = unbroken; $\Gamma_{\max} > 0$ = broken); stable Kerr waveform amplitudes ($\sigma_f^{	ext{max}}$).
important_parameters: Gain/loss strength ($\gamma$), coupling width ($W$), peak coupling amplitude ($\kappa_0$), and nonlinear coefficients ($\sigma,  eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations for different coupling widths (homogeneous vs. finite width) and the nonlinear stability assessment is limited to a specific adiabatic ramping protocol.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spectral scans showing re-entrant unbroken–broken–unbroken PT sequences by varying parameters, and show the adiabatic generation of Kerr states from linear seeds.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the linear eigenproblem in various coupling limits (homogeneous vs. finite width) to mapping out phase diagrams exhibiting re-entrant transitions; it then extends this analysis into the nonlinear regime using adiabatic propagation to find stable, persistent waveforms.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from PT-symmetry breaking and topological phase transitions with spatial engineering in coupled optical systems, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum optical components.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic representation of two locally coupled ring resonators. Ring 1 carries linear gain +γ, ring 2 carries the balanced linear loss −γ, and the real inter-ring coupling is concentrated in a finite angular sector described by Eq. (3).

Figure 2: Hermitian spectrum at κ0 = 0.9 and γ = 0. The two dashed outer branches are the homogeneous-coupling values, each retaining the ±n degeneracy. For the local profile with W = 1.8, each excited doublet is resolved into four parity-dependent branches. Broadening the coupling region suppresses the nonzero Fourier harmonics and recombines these branches into the homogeneous spectrum.

Figure 3: Real parts of the non-Hermitian spectrum at κ0 = 0.9 and γ = 0.2, comparing the local profile with W = 2.2 and the homogeneous limit. Local coupling again resolves each excited doublet into four branches. The annotated pairs have coincident real parts and nonzero imaginary parts of opposite sign in the full numerical spectrum; they therefore represent broken-PT complex-conjugate eigenvalues.

Figure 4: Six lowest Hermitian eigenvalues versus coupling width at κ0 = 0.9 and γ = 0. All branches remain real; symmetry-distinct states cross without coalescence. The large- and small-W limits approach Eqs. (15) and (18), respec- tively.

Figure 5: Real parts of the six lowest non-Hermitian eigenvalues versus coupling width at κ0 = 0.9 and γ = 0.2. Dashed segments mark complex-conjugate pairs with equal real parts and opposite imaginary parts. Their endpoints are exceptional points. A detailed view of the evolution of the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenstates is provided in the Supplementary Movies S1–S2.
